fields.h1: Build a Membership Form With Tiers and Renewal Reminders
fields.hero_description: Build a membership form that sets dues by tier, takes a signature, and saves every member to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Members Complete and What Follows
fields.features_subheading: Members see each tier's price and sign before they submit. Alerts and renewal emails keep your membership desk on schedule.
fields.feature_1:
Tiers that set the yearly dues

Each membership level shows its yearly dues beside it, whether Individual, Family, Student, or one you name. The level a member picks is saved on their record with its dues.
fields.feature_2:
A row for each household member

Choosing a family tier opens a section with a name and birth date row for every extra person. One record then holds the whole household, and nobody in it fills in a second form.
fields.feature_3:
The club rules, signed on the last screen

Members read your bylaws or code of conduct before they submit and sign in a box under the text. The signature and its date are saved on the same row as the application.
fields.feature_4:
An alert for every new application

Each new application emails your membership secretary or posts to a Slack channel. One left unopened for 3 days triggers a reminder, then moves up to your board chair.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders before a membership lapses

Members get an email ahead of their renewal date, on a schedule you set. Anyone who still has not renewed goes to your membership desk by email or Slack for a follow-up.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take to GitHub

Move the full code into your GitHub repository on paid plans. From there the form can sit inside your existing site, and every later change can be reviewed as a pull request.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Organizations, Four Kinds of Member
fields.tab_content_1:
Her dues fall to $30 after the app reads her card

Tamsin Okafor applies to the Brightwater Society of Engineers as a student and uploads her student ID. The app reads her school, Ferncliff Technical College, and the card's expiry date, June 2027, into her application. A current card puts her on the $30 student rate instead of the $140 full rate.
fields.tab_content_2:
Dario's Family tier covers 4 players with its $420 dues

Dario Benedetti joins Linden Park Tennis Club on the Family tier and adds 3 household members: Ines, Luca, and Sofia. The form gives each of them a row for a name and birth date. All 4 players sit on a single membership record at $420 a year, and the front desk sees the whole household on that record.
fields.tab_content_3:
Slack shows the desk request that Jonah approves

Nadia Ferreira applies for a dedicated desk at Foundry Row Cowork and asks to start on November 3. Her application posts to the new-members Slack channel with her desk type, start date, and company, Quarry Lane Design. Community manager Jonah Price opens it from the message and approves her that afternoon.
fields.tab_content_4:
Unrenewed after 14 days means a call from the desk

Five Ashgrove Museum memberships expire in November, and each member gets a renewal email 30 days before the date. Four renew from the link in that email. Lorna Whitcombe has not renewed 14 days later, and her name moves to the membership desk's call list with her Patron tier.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Membership Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a membership form that knows each tier's dues and reminds every member before renewal.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List your tiers and who qualifies
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down every membership level, its yearly dues, and who qualifies for it, such as students with a current ID. Add the length of a membership term and when renewals fall due. You will paste that list into the prompt next.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Tell Emergent in plain English which tiers you offer, what each new member fills in, and who handles new applications. Emergent builds the form, the member database, and the logic that ties each tier to its dues. Prompt again to change a tier or a field.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick the tiers that need a document, such as a student card or a professional license. Have the app read the expiry date from each upload, and send any reading it is unsure of to your membership secretary before the rate applies.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste the rules members agree to onto the last screen, with the signature box right under them. Keep that text short enough to read on a phone, and link the full bylaws when they run longer than a page.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose how far ahead of the renewal date the first email goes out and what happens when nobody responds. For an annual membership, start with an email at 30 days and a call list at 14; shorten both for monthly plans.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Submit one individual, one family with 3 household members, and one student with an expired card. Then open the database and check that each row holds the right tier, the household names, the signature, and the dues.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish and retire the paper version
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the form on a custom domain, which Emergent includes and which uses credits. Link it from your join page and from each renewal email, and stop handing out paper membership forms once the online one is live.

faq_plan.a: A membership form is the document a club, association, or nonprofit uses to sign up a new member. Organizations use membership forms to record who each person is, which level they chose, the dues that level carries, and their signed agreement to the rules. The completed form becomes that member's record.

faq_plan.q: How to make a membership form?
faq_plan.ref: How to make a membership form?

prov.original: How to make a membership form?

faq_plan.a: List your tiers, the details you need from each member, and who reviews new signups, then describe that to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English. Emergent builds the form, the logic between tiers, and the database every member lands in. Share the link once a test signup lands in the database the way you expect.

faq_plan.q: What is the format of a membership registration form?
faq_plan.ref: What is the format of a membership registration form?

prov.original: What is the format of a membership registration form?

faq_plan.a: A membership registration form runs in five parts, in this order: contact details, the membership tier and term, household members where the tier allows them, the signed agreement, and an office-use block for the approval date and member number. Keep the same order on any printed membership form PDF, and paper signups will match the online ones.

faq_plan.q: What is the address label on a membership form?
faq_plan.ref: what is address label in pmi membership form
faq_plan.a: It is the tag that says what kind of address you entered, such as Home or Business. The organization uses it to send mail and renewal notices to the right one, and when a form asks for two addresses, the label marks the mailing address. A rental application form asks for past addresses instead, each with the dates you lived there.

faq_plan.q: How do I cancel a membership I joined with a membership form?
faq_plan.ref: how can i cancel membership form course hero
faq_plan.a: Check the agreement section of the form you signed, if it has one: that is where an organization states who receives a cancellation, how much notice it needs, and whether paid dues come back. Send your notice in writing to that person or address, keep a copy, and ask for a reply that confirms the end date.

faq_plan.q: What cancellation terms belong on a membership form?
faq_plan.ref: how can i cancel membership form coursehero
faq_plan.a: Put three on it: how a member cancels, how much notice you need, and what happens to dues already paid. Place them directly above the signature box, where members read them before they sign. On Emergent, one new prompt changes those terms, and the next signup sees the new wording.

faq_plan.q: Is a membership application form different from a membership form?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the organization approves members before they join; otherwise the two names describe the same form. A membership application form adds a decision step, where a secretary or committee checks each applicant against the criteria and accepts or declines. A job application form follows the same pattern, with every applicant waiting on a decision.

faq_plan.q: Should I start from a membership form template?
faq_plan.a: Only as a checklist. A membership form template carries another organization's tiers, prices, and rules, and you will change each of them before your first signup. Starting from your own list of levels and agreement text is faster, and a form built on Emergent has no response caps, even when every member renews in the same month.

faq_plan.q: How much does a membership form cost?
faq_plan.ref: how much is apc membership form
faq_plan.a: There is no standard price: the organization that issues a membership form sets any fee for it. Ask that organization for its current fee before you pay anyone for a copy. If you are the one issuing it, Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing a membership form.

faq_plan.q: What should a gym membership form include?
faq_plan.ref: how to cancel la fitness membership form
faq_plan.a: A gym membership form needs contact details, an emergency contact, the plan and its billing date, a health or liability acknowledgment, and the date the plan renews. If you photograph members for your website or social posts, collect that consent on a separate photo release form instead of burying it in the membership terms.

findings.issue: Divit's relevance rule (2026-10-15): every FAQ question serves someone building or running the form; a question for the person who filled it in is a finding. This one is for the member ('Check the agreement section of the form you signed... Send your notice in writing'), as the writer's own note says. FAQ 6 already serves the builder side of the same source keyword.
findings.fix: Swap for a builder-side question (e.g. how to set renewal reminders, which fields a membership form needs); if none passes, park per the A6 default.

findings.quote: What is the address label on a membership form?
findings.issue: Same class: answered to the member ('the tag that says what kind of address you entered'), from the keyword 'what is address label in pmi membership form', which is about filling in one association's form. The answer is also an unsourced guess about what that label means, and it ends on an unrelated link sentence ('A rental application form asks for past addresses instead...').

findings.quote: How much does a membership form cost?

findings.fix: Swap for a builder-side question, or reword to the issuer's cost question with the answer led by it.
